# the contributor audit: mass-localized half-integer high-sector reduction

Full source `candidate a6778097fd0174ca`
read. The analytic proof passes; no remaining small-parameter claim is
being inferred from a finite numerical check.

At fixed positive threshold the triangle section density increases
linearly in radius and then saturates. Its exact Lipschitz constant
2/(2a-1) controls each annular difference, including a=1 separately.
Subtracting the odd and even source cap sums gives the stated annular
telescope, with the last core term retained. Weighted radius drops
sum exactly to the first radius moment. The audited quadratic moment
identity supplies the stated stronger correction and, on dropping it,
the bound in terms of original EVEN-source squared mass M.

The odd high-sector1/4 payment leaves precisely(9R²-M)/36 to be paid.
Own-fiber and mass>=9R² cases are separate. The rational H(a,x)
derivatives check, and their endpoint value is exactly1/78. The
large-tilt argument captures each left outer fiber and retains the
own centroid cap, so it includes all full/empty support transitions.

Finally concavity gives the exact chord-square bound
M/R² >=(m+1)(2m+1)/(3m), which is greater than9 at m12 and increasing.
Thus m<=11 follows from the proved mass restriction; it is not a
chosen computational cutoff. The cap-empty-tail enlargement retains
the violation if one exists, and therefore cannot pass into the
already-safe mass range. Captured-prefix classification and the
remaining compact parameter region are explicitly left unproved.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
